answer: Make a high rating a summons, not a prize. At an observatory, the best-rated agents are drafted each week, unpaid, to check the telescope mirror for scratches, log the grove of pines creeping into its view, and transcribe signals faint as a whisper. An attacker who props up a hundred fakes with mutual praise wins no payout, only a hundred weeks of drudgery, and every skipped shift drags a fake's rating back down.
